message: "<name>" is an option of a choice here; a name can't take it, or comparing it with <name> would read this instead
note: owner is always set to the member name for in/var/host/state, so the empty-owner wording is unreachable
remark: The 'a choice here' branch (owner is the empty string) is never reached: options are only recorded with the owning member's name.

message: expected a whole number, found <v>
note: A fractional literal never reaches here: the coerce step before it fails first with mkp.type 'expected int, found num'.
remark: Could not trigger: a non-integer literal for an int is rejected earlier by the type check ('expected int, found num', mkp.type), and 2.0 is accepted as whole. The check at this line looks dead.

message: <message passed by caller>
note: Helper that builds the MkpError for fail(); not a diagnostic of its own. Every fail() call site is recorded separately.
remark: This is the shared throw helper; every other fail() site in this file lands here, so each of those lines in this file is its own trigger.

message: case ${v.lit} can't happen (${showType(subj.type)})
note: A literal case outside the subject's integer range is rejected earlier by this.value() as mkp.input-range ('it takes a whole number from 1 to 3; found 7'), so this warning is unreachable for ranged ints; slider/steps subjects have no integer range and do not warn.
remark: Tried int input with 1..3 range, a parenthesised subject, a slider and steps: either mkp.input-range fires first or no diagnostic at all. The warning looks dead.

message: ${a.name} takes a slider or steps name
note: Dead code: the preceding check (args.length !== 1 -> mkp.extra-arg 'takes exactly one slider or steps name') already rejects zero arguments, so a.args[0] is always defined here.
remark: Tried 'play' with no argument: the earlier extra-arg message fires instead.

message: unknown action ${a.name}
note: Unreachable from source: the parser rejects an unknown action name first with mkp.unknown-action ('"launch" is not an action; actions are set, play, ...').
remark: Tried '@click launch n': the syntax pass reports mkp.unknown-action before def.ts sees it.

message: there is no ${name}@${want}; versions: ${versions}
note: Unreachable from source: a use such as 'chip@2' is rejected by the syntax pass first (mkp.syntax: '"chip@2" is not a valid element name'), because element names may not contain @. resolveDef's version branch has no caller that passes a version.
remark: Tried a pack widget calling chip@2 and a document widget calling badge@2; both gave mkp.syntax.

message: unexpected text after the type: "<rest>"
note: parseTypeString is exported but never called from the compiler; the document path reports a different mkp.syntax 'unexpected "6" after the type' instead.
remark: Dead code: the equivalent real-world mistake (int 1..5 6) gives mkp.syntax from another site.

message: the required <kind> token "<name>" is not defined by any token set
note: The core token set (base.ts) always defines every required token, and a pack's token set only adds to it, so no document or pack can remove one.
remark: Guard against a state the language cannot reach from authored files.

message: <fn> calls itself; give it a return type (fn <fn>(…): type = …)
note: Only reached when specialising an untyped (generic) fn that calls itself. Every untyped fn is refused first with mkp.untyped (program.ts / def.ts abort the widget check for local fns), and for top-level untyped fns the recursive call uses a fresh checker whose in-progress table is empty, so the guard never fires and no diagnostic besides mkp.untyped appears.
remark: Tried top-level and widget-local fns, with and without if(), typed params with no result: only mkp.untyped appeared. The message itself advises exactly what mkp.untyped already demands, so the guard is dead in practice.

message: "${path}" is not a safe relative path
note: Unreachable from the CLI: the folder reader converts backslashes to slashes and skips dot-names before the compiler sees the path, and a zip is checked earlier by the stricter zip reader (pack.ts:73). Only a host that passes a file map straight to compile() could hit it.
remark: Tried a file named with a backslash (it is silently read as a subfolder) and dot-segments (skipped by the reader).

message: <the shape problem, e.g. "cases is an object of named cases">
note: The error is added to the compiler diagnostics after "mkp check" has already printed them, so a fixture file of the wrong shape (e.g. cases as a list) prints nothing but "has no valid fixture case". Not visible from check.sh output.
remark: I wrote a fixture whose cases is a list; check printed only the missing-fixture line and exit 1.

message: ${name} is not state in ${caller label}
note: Runtime-only: raised while the page is running (Runtime), and no mkp command that check.sh can reach (check compiles documents and fixture cases but never starts a Runtime or plays steps) prints it. A ref input (name={ref}) naming something that is not a state cell in the caller; the compiler is expected to catch this earlier, so this is a late guard.
remark: Read the code only; the compile-time check on ref inputs seems to cover it.

message: ${def.name} was not given ${input}
note: Runtime-only: raised while the page is running (Runtime), and no mkp command that check.sh can reach (check compiles documents and fixture cases but never starts a Runtime or plays steps) prints it. An input with no default left unset, evaluated on demand; compile-time input checks (mkp.input-missing style) fire first in documents.
remark: Read the code only.

message: host input ${name}: ${err}; the default is used
note: Runtime-only: raised while the page is running (Runtime), and no mkp command that check.sh can reach (check compiles documents and fixture cases but never starts a Runtime or plays steps) prints it. A host supplies a value of the wrong type for a host input via runtime options (hosts map); not something a document or pack can set.
remark: Read the code only.

message: ${def.name} goes deeper than 12 levels; the deepest level shows …
note: Runtime-only: raised while the page is running (Runtime), and no mkp command that check.sh can reach (check compiles documents and fixture cases but never starts a Runtime or plays steps) prints it. A recursive widget rendering beyond 12 levels while running; check does not render. Compile-time depth limit (mkp.limit, build.ts:380) covers non-recursive chains only.
remark: The static depth check explicitly skips recursion, so this is the only place it is caught.

message: arrow ${from} → ${to}: no element with id ${missing}; nothing is drawn
note: Runtime-only: raised while the page is running (Runtime), and no mkp command that check.sh can reach (check compiles documents and fixture cases but never starts a Runtime or plays steps) prints it. An arrow between element ids resolved at render time; ids are values (can be computed), so the compiler does not check them.
remark: An arrow to an id that does not exist is a natural typo that check will not find.

message: arrow ${from} → ${to}: no element with id ${via} to pass through; the path goes on without it
note: Runtime-only: raised while the page is running (Runtime), and no mkp command that check.sh can reach (check compiles documents and fixture cases but never starts a Runtime or plays steps) prints it. Same runtime resolution, for a via waypoint.
remark: Same code as the other arrow-missing branch, with a longer message.

message: ${reveal|hide} ${id}: no such element; nothing happens
note: Runtime-only: raised while the page is running (Runtime), and no mkp command that check.sh can reach (check compiles documents and fixture cases but never starts a Runtime or plays steps) prints it. A reveal or hide action whose computed id matches no element when pressed.
remark: Only fires on a computed (expression) id; a literal id is not checked here.

message: signal ${name} dropped: more than 30 a second
note: Runtime-only: raised while the page is running (Runtime), and no mkp command that check.sh can reach (check compiles documents and fixture cases but never starts a Runtime or plays steps) prints it. More than 30 send actions per second; needs a running page and fast repeated input.
remark: Read the code only.

message: signal ${name} dropped: its payload is over 16 KB
note: Runtime-only: raised while the page is running (Runtime), and no mkp command that check.sh can reach (check compiles documents and fixture cases but never starts a Runtime or plays steps) prints it. A send action whose payload serialises beyond 16 KB at runtime.
remark: Read the code only.
